children: Bitmain is further cementing its dominance in the Bitcoin mining equipment market. As mining profitability deteriorates, rival manufacturers are cutting external sales or pivoting to artificial intelligence, narrowing the supply base for mining rigs.

Bitcoin.com reported on November 21 that Bitmain accounted for 82% of the mining equipment market as of June 2024, citing the Cambridge Digital Mining Industry Report. Since then, competitors have scaled back sales and shifted their businesses, further weakening suppliers once seen as challengers to Bitmain.

Bitdeer has stopped large-scale external sales and is focusing on its own mining operations. Bellagora AI, formerly known as Auradine, has shifted its business toward AI chip development. Canaan's third-quarter revenue from mining machine sales also plunged 96% from a year earlier.

Proto, the mining-rig brand owned by Jack Dorsey's Block, has also been hit by order cancellations. Its largest customer, Core Scientific, paid $42 million to withdraw from the contract. Manufacturers once viewed as alternatives to Bitmain are increasingly struggling to sell equipment.

Behind the shift is worsening profitability for mining companies. Hashprice, a measure of expected mining revenue for a given amount of computing power, fell to a record low in June. CoinShares said the average cost for listed miners to produce one Bitcoin in the second quarter was $75,500, exceeding Bitcoin's average price of $58,400 during the same period.

On a May earnings call, Bitdeer Chief Executive Officer Jihan Wu said weak Bitcoin prices meant the company would have to sell mining machines at very low prices, explaining its decision to halt external sales.

Whether competitors will resume sales remains uncertain. Leo Li, Bitdeer's head of U.S. sales, said the company would decide whether to restart external sales based on market conditions, production capacity and business priorities.

title: Bitmain Tightens Grip on Bitcoin Mining Rig Market as Rivals Retreat
